source_title: JulioFerrero/pocket-foundry: Play your own copy of Factorio on Android: the official Linux ARM64 build, run without emulation on the phone's GPU, with an on-screen controller. - GitHub
source_excerpt:
Play your own copy of Factorio on Android. The official Linux ARM64 build runs on the phone itself: no emulation, no streaming, no game files in the app.
Buy Factorio and download the Linux (arm64) .tar.xz from factorio.com/download .
Open Pocket Foundry, tap Import Factorio and pick the file.
Continue your newest save or open the Main menu .
Pocket Foundry ships one GPU driver, Turnip, and tests it on Adreno 6xx and newer. Other GPUs can use a community driver, made and tested by others, or run the game on the phone's CPU.
Loads, but slow? It's probably on the CPU, because the phone has no GPU driver yet. Settings -> Driver shows which one is in use. Phones and drivers has the community drivers and the phones people report working.
Playing : controls, controllers, settings, saves and game files
Something wrong, or it works on your phone? Open an issue with what the Logs screen shows (its Copy button takes it all).
GPL-3.0, as Termux:X11 is. Also bundled: glibc (LGPL-2.1), Mesa (MIT), SDL (zlib), liblzma (0BSD), Titillium Web (OFL-1.1), Apache Commons Compress and AndroidX (Apache-2.0).
Factorio is © Wube Software. Pocket Foundry isn't affiliated with Wube and includes none of its files; the game screenshots, the launcher's panels and buttons and the Home screen show art from the player's own copy.
Play your own copy of Factorio on Android: the official Linux ARM64 build, run without emulation on the phone's GPU, with an on-screen controller.
